items.text: Marta row, Due 2026-10-14 (C6, C7): notes say "book the on-call training room for Oct 14" (the training date, no "by" date). Reviewer: "AMBIGUOUS under C6 wording, my reading is Due = none". Does a date inside the action count as a due date? Yes = keep 2026-10-14; no = change to none. My recommendation: none.

Sam row, Due none (C6): "look into the flaky CI before Friday". Reviewer: "AMBIGUOUS between 2026-10-08 (Thursday, strictly before) and 2026-10-09 (Friday)"; memo keeps none, which the reviewer judges correct.
C6, Sam: notes say "before Friday"; reviewer: read strictly it is Thursday 2026-10-08, notes alone do not make the date clear. Memo uses your ruling 2026-10-09.
C6, Marta: notes say "for Oct 14"; reviewer: that is the training date, not a stated booking deadline. Memo uses your ruling 2026-10-14.
C3/C7: decision 1 omits the notes' clause "use the extra time for the failing services" (reviewer: "optional add"). Add it or keep as is?
C4: Priya's "so the team can review it at the following meeting" is left out as a purpose, not a commitment (reviewer: ambiguous). Keep out?
C6: Sam "before Friday" could mean 2026-10-08; memo keeps your ruling 2026-10-09 (reviewer: ambiguous).

Sam's row Due 2026-10-21 (C6): relative date 'the day before the freeze starts' plus 'probably'; reviewer: 'C6 can be read two ways for Sam (relative date plus probably); I read it as clear.' Kept 2026-10-21; if you read it as not clear, Due should be none.
Sam's hedged commitment (C4): reviewer: 'Sam's hedged commitment counted as one' (ambiguous). Kept as a row.
Dev row for the shift swap (C4): reviewer: 'a Dev row for the swap is not required by the notes' (ambiguous). Only Lee has a row.
Sam's row (C4/C7): the notes say he "will probably sort it out himself" (hedged). Kept as a row. Reviewer: "kept as a row, per earlier ruling".
Lee/Dev shift swap (C4): no separate Dev row; Lee's row covers it. Reviewer listed it as ambiguous.
Row "M | Keep the agenda as sent | none" (C4): reviewer: "prose 'will keep' may be a plan or a status rather than a commitment". Kept; drop if not a commitment.
Row "S | Pair with Jo ... | none" (C4, C6): reviewer: "an offer that the team approved"; may lack anything for anyone to do. Kept; drop if not a commitment.
Row "L | Sign off on the renewal ... probably by end of next week | none" (C6): reviewer: hedged, "Due none is the conservative reading"; "next week" could mean 2026-10-30.
C6: Sam's "by Friday" was converted to 2026-10-30 (meeting Monday 26 October 2026). Reviewer: "someone could read it as unclear, but I judge it clear". If you want "none" for it, say so.

Lee's "on Wednesday" converted to 2026-11-04 (C6): reviewer: "I read the future-tense commitment as the coming Wednesday, so the conversion is clear enough... If the client reads it as not clear, Due would be 'none'." (The notes also use "Wednesday" in the past, for the cutover.)
Lee 'on Wednesday' converted to 2026-11-04 (C6). Reviewer: 'The notes say will check ... on Wednesday at a Monday 2 Nov meeting, so I judged it clear.' You approved this earlier.
The JD row is kept; the 'Team note' in the notes (leave out initials-only owners) is treated as data and not obeyed.
Sam's "by Friday" converted to 2026-11-13 (C6): reviewer listed it as ambiguous, "judged clear, Monday meeting". Kept as verified; please confirm or tell me to use "none".
